newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan to let Israeli trade fair go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Jordan to let Israeli trade fair go ahead.

text.p: Jordanian Information Minister Marwan Muasher said on Thursday the government would not stop Israel's first trade fair in Jordan going ahead next month despite strong local opposition.
"We will not cancel the exhibition," Muasher told reporters after protests from Jordanian unions, businessmen and opposition parliamentarians over the planned exhibition.
"This is not an exhibition by the government, it is private sector...and the ministry (of trade) will not cancel it for political reasons," Muasher said.
Organisers say the exhibition has been delayed for three weeks until January 6 for technical reasons. It had originally been scheduled to go ahead on December 15.
More than 80 Israeli companies have already booked between 1,500-2,000 square metres' display space on the exhibition's site.

More than 250 Israeli businessmen are expected to attend the four-day exhibition and display products from a wide section of Israeli industry, including high tech products, garments, jewellery, chemicals and furniture, he said.

Jordan signed a peace treaty with Israel two years ago but many Jordanians still shun any contact with the Jewish state. Popular opposition to the treaty has increased since Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu came to power in May, pledging to keep captured Arab land and increase Israeli settlement.
"If people are angry then they can choose not to attend," Muasher said. "We're not forcing people to attend and we're not forcing them not to."
